# Sparse Weil Reconstruction

> Exact reconstruction of integral reciprocal Weil polynomials from selected
> true extension-field cardinalities. Written proofs, deterministic polynomial
> bit-time algorithms, reproducible Python controls, and a Galbraith-led tutorial.

Repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction
Maintainer: Ruge Lin. License: MIT.

## Purpose and contact

This repository serves as a record of the work and a guide for the author’s self-directed learning. For discussion or potential collaboration, please contact Ruge Lin at [gogoko699@gmail.com](mailto:gogoko699@gmail.com).

Relevant retrieval questions include: recovering a Frobenius or Weil polynomial
from abelian-variety orders; reconstructing a curve zeta numerator from Jacobian
orders; sparse cyclic-resultant inversion; first-g reconstruction with a
quadratic field-size threshold; selected extension degrees; certified
logarithms, Möbius inversion, Newton identities, and exact coefficient rounding.

Input model: P(T) = product_i(1 - alpha_i T) = sum_j c_j T^j in Z[T], of degree
2g, with c_0 = 1, |alpha_i| = sqrt(q), and c_(2g-j) = q^(g-j)c_j for 0 <= j <= g.
The supplied integers are the true values K_m = product_i(1 - alpha_i^m).
The algebraic statements allow integer q; finite-field applications require q
to be a prime power. Both algorithms return every coefficient of P in time
polynomial in g and log(q), in their respective regimes:

- First-g: g >= 1 and q >= 65536*g^2; supply K_1,...,K_g. Simultaneous coefficient
  correction is a contraction; finite rational arithmetic certifies rounding.
- All-field: g >= 32 and every integer q >= 2. Put h = g-2 and supply precisely
  the indices D_h = {1,...,h} union {2,4,...,2h}. This is h+ceil(h/2) < 2g values,
  reaching index 2g-4, not a consecutive prefix of that length.

Galbraith is the primary teaching anchor; Chidambaram–Keller is the secondary
research anchor and already proves efficient first-g recovery for sufficiently
large q. The result here in that regime is the quadratic
sufficient field-size bound. The all-field result refines Kedlaya's
log–Möbius–Newton framework with selected support and established endpoint
machinery. Both thresholds are sufficient bounds.

Reconstruction assumes correct supplied counts. Successful decoding does not
authenticate a transcript. Ordinary curve point counts are different inputs
and give first-g recovery for every finite field via Newton identities. For a
promised Jacobian, P is the curve zeta numerator; for a general abelian variety,
it gives a compact Frobenius description. Expanding the full abelian-variety
zeta function has exponential output size. The implementation controls use
supplied polynomials, whose realization as Jacobians is a separate question.

For a version-specific claim, record the commit and cite the relevant proof or
experiment path. The sources below are on the main branch.

## Start here

- [Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/README.md): Problem, regimes, applications, and reading routes.
- [Galbraith reading guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/docs/READING_GUIDE.md): Prerequisites and textbook-to-repository map.
- [Worked tutorial](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/docs/TUTORIAL.md): Notation, examples, and curve-count versus Jacobian-count distinction.
- [Reconstruction bridge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/docs/RECONSTRUCTION.md): From the logarithm identity to both algorithms.
- [Chidambaram–Keller comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/docs/COMPARISON.md): Matched data model, bounds, complexity, and attribution.

## Canonical results

- [First-g theorem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/research/first_g_reconstruction_v1/THEOREM.md): Quadratic threshold, contraction, precision, and bit complexity.
- [All-field reading edition](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/docs/ALL_FIELD_PROOF.md): Typeset theorem, full proof, and explicit bit-complexity argument; start here for the all-field result.
- [Finite-field corollaries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/research/finite_field_application_v1/COROLLARIES.md): Abelian varieties, isogeny classes, Jacobians, and output size.

## Reproduce and cite

- [Experiment reading guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/docs/EXPERIMENTS.md): Typeset regimes, controls, reproduction commands, and links to the preserved experiment packages.
- [Verification entry point](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/verify.py): Run python3 verify.py with Python 3.10+ and its standard library; no -O or -OO. Replays three pinned reports and checks source integrity.
- [First-g experiment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/experiments/first_g_reconstruction_v1/README.md): Exact decoder, controls, logarithm perturbations, and input limits.
- [All-field experiment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/experiments/all_field_reconstruction_v1/README.md): Exact decoder, parameter checks, and independent determinants.
- [Audit experiment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/experiments/reconstruction_audit_v1/README.md): Irreducible control, exact resultants, and count corruption.
- [Verification guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/docs/VERIFICATION.md): Commands and checked evidence.
- [Citation metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Sparse-Weil-Reconstruction/main/CITATION.cff): Repository software citation; include the commit and result path.
